blindReviewDeclaration: Fresh v2s-rooted independent review first reopened every mandatory input, recomputed the declared hashes, ran both required six-dimension routes, and formed the findings and NO_GO verdict before reading any author self-review, finding disposition, or round-1 intake. The author intake was read only afterwards for difference reporting and was not treated as authority.

riskClasses: owner authorization, actor snapshot, face projection, and sensitive-data containment

expectedBehavior: R5 remains design-only: implementation, runtime, and seed/reset are false until the stated review and Dexter-acceptance chain completes.
Each Part C rule is referenced by its real C.T01 through C.T23 matrix identifier and remains review-routed, not disguised as a semantic gate.
Every carried/adapted page, feature, app shell, and foundation asset has a source-path/hash, target path, owning app, explicit disposition, retained boundary, and focused evidence responsibility.

getEntityAuditHistory is one dual-face task read for the approved twelve entity types; host read authorization precedes owner-local audit reading, and the response exposes only face-projected command-time display snapshots and human-readable safe diffs.

findings.title: Manifest Part C does not bind any real C.T matrix rule
findings.evidence: The manifest records only C.T01-C.T06, C.T07-C.T12, C.T13-C.T19, and C.T20-C.T23. Fresh exact lookup against contracts/policy/standards-coverage-matrix.json found no ruleId for any of those four strings; the matrix instead contains the twenty-three individual ruleIds C.T01 through C.T23. standards-coverage --phase R5 passed because it validates the matrix denominator, not this manifest-to-matrix reference relation.
findings.risk: The design claims all Part C coverage but supplies no stable actual-ID trace from any delivery unit to the rule and its review destination. A later reviewer cannot tell which of the twenty-three reference-pattern obligations applies, while a green coverage command can be misreported as proof of that absent mapping.
findings.disposition: Before any further review or implementation decision, replace the four range tokens with the actual individual C.T01-C.T23 IDs, map each to the applicable delivery unit and its review checklist/source anchor, and re-run the existing coverage and granularity checks. This is a manifest-only trace repair; it must not create a semantic keyword gate or alter the frozen matrix.

findings.title: Carry-over-first is asserted but no implementation-facing carry/adapt inventory exists
findings.evidence: The revised design says the 22 surfaces and 25 pageDesignKeys continue to rely on accepted artifacts and a frozen frontend manifest, while R5-U07 contains only three broad feature/foundation directories. Neither reviewed document contains the required per-page/feature/app-shell/foundation sourcePath@hash, targetPath, owning app, CARRY/ADAPT/REWRITE/NOT_APPLICABLE disposition, retained boundary, or focused evidence mapping. The only concrete audit screen records NO_V2_COUNTERPART, which cannot inventory the remaining approved UI assets.
findings.risk: An implementer must rediscover the v2 baseline and decide carry versus rewrite during implementation. That defeats the mandatory carry-over-first control, permits accidental shell/foundation duplication or missed pages, and means the claimed 22/25 denominator is not an implementation-ready plan.
findings.disposition: Add one bounded manifest inventory for the already approved 22 surfaces/25 page keys and the two app shells/foundation consumers. It should reference existing frozen interaction assets rather than redraw UI, and for each asset state source hash, target, app owner, disposition, retained/non-inherited boundary, and L2/L3 evidence. The accepted audit Modal remains one NO_V2_COUNTERPART entry with its stated new-scope reason.

findings.title: Current manifest cannot pass the production granularity validator
findings.evidence: Fresh execution of scripts/check/implementation-design-granularity with the current manifest and this review fails closed with UNIT_SOURCE_R5-U08_2_ANCHOR_NOT_UNIQUE:0. R5-U08 binds doc/decisions/2026-07-24-v2s-verification-governance.md to the anchor # V2S 验证治理, but the frozen document's actual unique heading is # 验证工作的通用规则.
findings.risk: The proposed design package has no runnable production binding proof. Its stated managed-DEV, seed, L2/L3, and cleanup unit can therefore reach neither the checker nor a trustworthy implementation-facing handoff.
findings.disposition: Correct the manifest source anchor to the exact frozen heading and re-run the unchanged production validator with this review. Do not weaken the anchor-uniqueness control or change the frozen verification decision.

findings.title: Production granularity validation is healthy but is not proof of the two missing design relations
findings.evidence: scripts/check/implementation-design-granularity --self-test fresh passed all declared red fixtures, including hash drift, missing evidence, review-round, input-checklist, post-remediation, flow-name, and baseline-state controls. Its production implementation validates manifest structure, hashes, anchors, units, review links, and severity counts, but does not read standardsCoverage.partC or test carry-over asset inventory. Consequently it can pass a review bound to the current manifest while M-001 and M-002 remain.
findings.risk: The validator may be cited beyond its mechanical scope, creating a false claim that it approved standards traceability or carry-over completeness.
findings.disposition: Keep the validator and its current controls; record its scope honestly in evidence. Resolve M-001 and M-002 through the design artifact and fresh human review rather than adding a semantic checker solely to satisfy this review.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The approved audit addition solves the user task of understanding who changed what while remaining in the current entity detail. Its single dual-face operation and Modal avoid a second permission model, twelve duplicated endpoints, a route, or a log browser.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: A live cross-owner identity lookup would be shorter to sketch but violates the owner and least-disclosure boundary; a global audit owner or copied identity projection would add an unnecessary fact owner and topology. The current command-time minimal display snapshot plus face projection is the smaller valid approach, provided host authorization is performed before owner task reading as stated.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The audit snapshot/projection design is proportionate and does not itself require a finding: it keeps audit facts owner-local, uses no new authorization, avoids sensitive identity fields, and preserves historical display after account changes. By contrast, missing actual C.T links and the required carry/adapt inventory leave mandatory design work to implementation, so their cost is not yet proportionate to an implementation-facing handoff.

conclusion.summary: Independent round 2 confirms Roadmap/current authorization consistency and finds the actor snapshot/face projection a bounded solution for the approved audit task. The revised design still cannot be handed off because it has no exact Part C C.T01-C.T23 trace, no mandatory carry-over-first implementation inventory, and a broken R5-U08 frozen-source anchor that makes the production granularity validator fail closed. M=3, S=0, N=1. This is a design review only.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: This verdict neither authorizes R5 implementation, runtime, DEV, seed/reset, contracts, migrations, tests, scripts, nor any source change. It only records the final independent adversarial review result for the current design bytes.

authorIntakeComparison.difference: The round-1 intake correctly repaired the prior C.TABLE aliases, Roadmap state, authorization metadata, and actor snapshot shape. This round independently found that the replacement Part C range tokens still are not actual matrix rule IDs, and that carry-over-first remains absent at implementation-facing asset granularity. The intake did not change this verdict.
